stories.headline: Premier League's summer transfer market is dangerously out of control
stories.summary: Liam Delap's big move to Nottingham Forest came with a fee that didn't make sense given his poor spell at Chelsea. Welcome to the new era of wild transfer spending and accounting.
stories.body:
Let's play a little Premier League numbers game, but the only guarantee is that the numbers won't add up.

It involves a deal worth up to £85 million for Sávio, a Manchester City squad player who joined Tottenham, a £50m transfer to Nottingham Forest for Liam Delap following an injury-hit year at Chelsea, and Tottenham's £85m deal for West Ham's Mateus Fernandes, a player whose unenviable claim to fame was that he suffered successive relegations with the Hammers and Southampton.

There are plenty more names to add to that list, including goalkeeper James Trafford, midfielder Elliot Anderson and playmaker Morgan Rogers, in a summer that has seen the transfer market in England lose all sense of proportion -- perhaps to a dangerous degree.

By the time the 2026 summer transfer window closed on Tuesday, the 20 Premier League teams had spent just over £3.4 billion combined on new signings -- a record that eclipsed last year's total of £3.2bn -- with four players (Enzo Fernández and Anderson to Man City, Bradley Barcola to Liverpool, Rogers to Chelsea) all moving for transfer fees in excess of £100m.

But rewind to early July, when the football world's sole focus was on the 2026 FIFA World Cup, and note the Annual Review of Football Finance published by Deloitte detailed that pre-tax losses among the Premier League's clubs had rocketed by more than 600%, with collective losses of £948m in the 2024-25 season, up from a relatively insignificant £135m a year earlier.

That's right. In the most up-to-date figures, not including two subsequent summer windows that saw over £3bn in spending, the richest league in the world is carrying losses approaching £1bn.

- Men's summer transfers: Grading every major move

- Transfer window winners and losers: Good for Chelsea, bad for Liverpool

- Ranked: Summer transfers most likely to fail

In April, Chelsea announced pre-tax losses of £262m -- a Premier League record -- for the 2024-25 season, with Spurs reporting a pre-tax loss of £120.6 million in March, and Manchester United reporting a loss of £39.7m. Even Manchester City posted losses of £9.m; of the Big Six, only Liverpool recorded a profit in their most recent financial figures of just £15.2m.

So it is against that backdrop that this summer's inexplicable spending has played out, largely, but not exclusively, by those heavyweight clubs.

Man City, Chelsea and Spurs have all spent over £300m this summer -- City set a new Premier League record by spending £458m -- but those headline figures have largely been offset by hefty incoming transfer fees, with City and Chelsea both raising more than £300m via outgoing deals. Yet despite the losses, Premier League clubs have spent big and fees in excess of £50m have become the norm.

Why are English clubs spending so heavily?

"If you look at the Premier League, a lot of the transfer money spent by those clubs is staying in the Premier League," a former Premier League sporting director told ESPN. "So that is driving up prices because despite the annual losses, clubs know that they each have cash flowing around due to their transfer dealings.

"The majority of Premier League clubs also want Premier League-proven players, which adds a premium to those players because there are only a finite number who tick that box. If they are young and English -- Anderson and Rogers, for example -- they have an even greater scarcity value."

To that point, City made a £13m profit on England goalkeeper Trafford by offloading him to Leeds for £40m after just one season as Gianluigi Donnarumma's understudy at the Etihad. Chelsea, meanwhile, made a £20m profit on Delap, despite the forward scoring just three goals in 49 appearances after his £30m move from Ipswich last summer.

"It's supply and demand," the former sporting director said. "Some clubs have discovered, to their cost, that signing players from outside the Premier League is a risk not worth taking. United have had their fingers burnt by signing players from Italy's Serie A -- ultimately, the Premier League is a crowded and over-heated market because clubs are increasingly only prepared to trade in their own league."

Some clubs, like Brentford and Brighton have developed successful recruitment models based on identifying emerging talent outside the Premier League. Mamadou Sangare, a £39m signing from Lens, has been outstanding in his early games for Brentford this season, while there is a belief at Brighton that Malick Yalcouyé, a modest £6m signing from IFK Gothenburg in 2024, could emulate Moisés Caicedo and Carlos Baleba, developing into a target for elite clubs after being spotted as youngster in Sweden, a relatively untapped league.

But few clubs are as well run as Brentford and Brighton, so they must strike a balance between gambles from overseas or paying inflated fees for Premier League players.

"The Rogers and Anderson deals were done quite early in the window, so those fees set a benchmark for the window," a former Premier League chief scout, now working in the English Football League, told ESPN. "That's why you have seen some ridiculous fees for players who are nowhere near worth the price that they have moved for.

"The market has also been impacted by big fees paid by Saudi Pro League clubs. If City are able to bank over £50m for Tijjani Reijnders [to Al Qadsiah] and make a profit after a pretty uninspiring season at the club, it makes everyone else bump up the valuations of their players. The problem for clubs below the Premier League is that very little of the money is trickling down to the EFL.

"It's all just circulating between the top clubs, and lots of the money is going out of the game on agents' fees rather than feeding the food chain."

Will there be a financial correction in forthcoming transfer windows? Possibly, but the likelihood is that clubs will keep on spending.

When even under-performing players can generate a profit for clubs due to the lack of alternative options in the market, the numbers are only going to rise. But that's the unique world of the Premier League, where losses and spending only go in the same unsustainable direction.

stories.headline: Why does the Italian GP trophy look like a pile of washing up?
stories.summary: The winner of this weekend's Italian Grand Prix will receive a trophy that looks like a pile of washing up after Pirelli commissioned two artists to come up with the design.
stories.body:
The winner of this weekend's Italian Grand Prix will receive a trophy that looks like a pile of washing up after Pirelli commissioned two artists to come up with the design.

For the past six years, Pirelli, the official sponsor of the Italian Grand Prix, has commissioned Italian artists to design the trophies presented to the top three drivers and winning constructor on Monza's famous podium.

This year the commission was awarded to Vedovamazzei, an art duo made up of Stella Scala and Simeone Crispino.

The trophy, named FRAGILE, is designed to look like a series of mugs and bowls precariously stacked on top of each other.

- Italian Grand Prix 2026: Race start time, how to watch, full schedule

- Ferrari to run Schumacher tribute livery at Monza

- Hamilton takes ownership of Ferrari F40 road car

Why is the trophy designed this way?
"One day, while putting a bowl in the sink, we suddenly realised that the trophy was right there in front of us," the artists said. "The sink saved the aesthetics of the piece."

The trophy is produced from nylon polymer using a 3D printing process before being painted, galvanized, and polished until it becomes reflective.

"The idea for the trophy stems from the ancient tradition of passing a celebratory cup from hand to hand. It served as a large drinking vessel, creating a sense of shared celebration and festivity."

"We wanted the trophy to be the symbol of a victory that an individual holds in their hands, yet it reflects the spirit of a community," the artists added. "In the case of Formula 1, this community includes the team, the fans, and the entire world revolving around the drivers.

"The composition also evokes an everyday dimension with its repeated gestures, suggesting a victory earned lap after lap that never corresponds to an eternal, unchanging status. It is unstable, short-lived, and must be reclaimed. In fact, it is fragile."

stories.headline: No shift on Swans suspension amid police investigation
stories.summary: Sydney's five exiled players will remain stood down until the end of the AFL season, regardless of how an ongoing police investigation unfolds.
stories.body:
Sydney's five exiled players will remain stood down until the end of the AFL season, regardless of how an ongoing police investigation unfolds.

Victoria Police have interviewed four Sydney men as part of an investigation into sexual assault allegations during a post-AFL match party at East Melbourne's Pullman Hotel.

Swans players Isaac Heeney, Chad Warner, Nick Blakey, Riley Bice and James Jordon were suspended for the remainder of the season for "breaching club standards" and will not be at the SCG for the club's qualifying final against Brisbane on Saturday.

Those suspensions are separate to the police investigation.

Swans coach Dean Cox reiterated those sanctions would remain unchanged despite police interviewing only four men.

Detectives confirmed they travelled to NSW this week to interview a 30-year-old Maroubra man, a 25-year-old Paddington man and two Randwick men aged 25 and 26.

No charges have been laid and AAP is not suggesting any wrongdoing on the part of the five suspended players.

"All five will remain stood down from the football club," Cox said on Thursday.

"That's one thing that we spoke about at the start, the police investigation and then the behavioural nature of it.

"We're going to be separated, and that will still remain."

Police have flagged that an update to the investigation is not expected for at least eight weeks.

Cox - who has remained in contact with the five players over their wellbeing - said the timeframe was out of the club's control as they wrestle with making a call on the group's playing future.

The eight-week period takes in the free agency and trade period from October 2 to October 14.

"That's part of the investigation of the way they do it. I just focus on what we can control and what I can control," Cox said.

Asked about potential impacts on the club's trade period, the Swans coach was short: "There are so many things that we need to talk about, so not for today."

While Sydney club chairman Andrew Pridham claimed the suspensions would "torpedo" the second-placed Swans' premiership hopes, Cox was adamant the playing group still had drive.

The Swans return to the SCG after a bye weekend following their emotional 53-point win over North Melbourne, where Cox and captain Callum Mills were in tears after the siren.

"There's still an expectation. You're hosting a qualifying final at home with a chance to go into a prelim, so there's still a hell of a lot at stake," Cox said.

"That's one thing that I want to make sure our players are aware of: the magnitude of this game for our football club and what we've spent so long trying to get to."

stories.headline: Aaron Rodgers: Steelers' 4-QB room is first of 22-year NFL career
stories.summary: The 42-year-old quarterback is in new territory, but he says Pittsburgh's young passers are ahead of where he was as a rookie.
stories.body:
PITTSBURGH -- Entering his 22nd year in the NFL, Aaron Rodgers is experiencing a first.

The Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback is one of four signal-callers on the 53-man roster, along with Mason Rudolph, Will Howard and Drew Allar, and Rodgers said Wednesday that he has never been part of a four-man QB room until now.

"I was thinking it was a possibility, but I don't think I've been on a roster with four quarterbacks," the 42-year-old said.

"Obviously when you do that, you're taking away a spot from another place in the team. But at the same time, if the best 53 are going to make it -- and not saying they did -- I think those four are part of the best 53."

It makes sense that Rodgers hasn't been part of a four-man quarterback room. Until this season, McCarthy had never had more than three quarterbacks on his teams' active rosters to start a season. Under coach Matt LaFleur, Rodgers was in a three-man quarterback room in 2020 after the Green Bay Packers drafted Jordan Love. Every other year under LaFleur, the team kept just two QBs. While Rodgers was with the New York Jets, he and Zach Wilson were the only quarterbacks on the 2023 Week 1 53-man roster. The next season, it was Rodgers and Tyrod Taylor.

Though Rodgers is in uncharted territory, he expressed excitement about working with the group.

"I'm happy for all those guys," Rodgers said. "Obviously looking to the future, those other three guys are going to have a chance when I'm done. And with the growth you saw with Will and obviously with Drew being drafted so high, but also playing well in camp, I'm not surprised at all and I'm excited about those guys' future."

Rodgers served as a mentor throughout the preseason, and he kept a close eye on Howard and Allar in the third preseason game at the Buffalo Bills as he watched from home.

"I'll keep some of the things that I was saying to the TV to myself," Rodgers said with a grin. "But no, I thought the entire camp, it was never too big for them. They looked really comfortable out there, and I thought they did a lot of good things moving the football, being efficient.

"There's learning experiences, but you look at my first preseason, it was not pretty at all. I didn't play good till about the second half of the fourth preseason game. So, they're definitely ahead of where I was at, and mentally, they're grasping the offense and the checks and the 'cans,' and I'm really proud about those guys."

stories.headline: 2026 FIBA Women's World Cup: Team USA analysis, rankings, rosters
stories.summary: Sixteen nations will compete in the World Cup in Berlin starting Friday. Team USA and France are front-runners.
stories.body:
The WNBA season is paused for the next couple of weeks, but there's plenty of women's basketball being played. The 2026 FIBA World Cup begins Friday and will run through Sept. 13 in Berlin, Germany. The tournament might not be as prominent as the Olympics -- to fans, at least -- but it is one of two major international competitions, with this year's event featuring 16 teams from North America, Europe, Asia and Africa.

The United States is, per usual, stacked, though the reigning champions suffered a blow when it was announced Monday that four-time WNBA MVP A'ja Wilson and five-time All-Star Kelsey Plum are unable to participate in the tournament due to health reasons. But those losses don't alter the task at hand: bringing home a fifth consecutive World Cup gold and 12th overall.

The U.S. women's national team plays its group phase opener Friday against China. The USA faces Italy on Sunday and then Czechia on Monday. If the U.S. women win their group, they move on to the quarterfinals on Sept. 10, with the semifinals set for Sept. 12 and the championship and third-place games on Sept. 13.

There are plenty of other familiar faces in Berlin, too, with dozens of current and former WNBA players representing other countries, from Australia to Türkiye.

ESPN's World Cup guide gets you set with everything you need to know before the games tip. Not every roster has been finalized yet, but we list current WNBA players on each squad, along with their stats for this current WNBA season.

Jump to:

HUN | ITA | JPN | KOR | MLI | NGR

PUR | ESP | TUR | USA | GROUPS

1. United States
Current WNBA players:

F/C Aliyah Boston, Indiana Fever (16.9 PPG, 8.3 RPG, 1.3 BPG)

G Caitlin Clark, Indiana Fever (22.5 PPG, 8.4 APG, 3.9 RPG)

F Napheesa Collier, Minnesota Lynx (18.0 PPG, 7.3 RPG, 1.4 SPG)

F/G Kahleah Copper, Phoenix Mercury (21.3 PPG, 3.6 RPG, 1.9 APG)

G Chelsea Gray, Las Vegas Aces (12.0 PPG, 6.8 APG, 1.4 SPG)

G Rhyne Howard, Atlanta Dream (18.3 PPG, 3.6 APG, 2.3 SPG)

F Kiki Iriafen, Washington Mystics (15.3 PPG, 9.4 RPG, 0.7 SPG)

F Angel Reese, Atlanta Dream (16.1 PPG, 12.4 RPG, 1.8 SPG)

F Breanna Stewart, New York Liberty (20.4 PPG, 8.1 RPG, 1.4 BPG)

G Jackie Young, Las Vegas Aces (18.9 PPG, 6.6 APG, 4.4 RPG)

Outlook: The U.S. women's national basketball team is home to one of the most dominant dynasties in all of sports, winning eight consecutive Olympic gold medals and four straight World Cups. The program has lost just one game at a major international competition since 1994 -- the semifinals of the 2006 World Championship (later renamed World Cup) against Russia, where the Americans won bronze. Team USA has since won 30 consecutive World Cup games.

That is the legacy newly minted national team director Sue Bird, senior national team coach Kara Lawson and this young U.S. squad -- a group with seven players under 27 -- bring to Berlin. Fans have long anticipated seeing the likes of Clark, Bueckers and Reese compete against international competition as part of the senior national team. They got a taste of that at the World Cup qualifying tournament, where the USA went 5-0 and won by an average margin of 42 points.

But between the grueling schedule, heighted competition and pressure of representing the USA, the World Cup will be a much greater challenge. USA Basketball's youth movement will be tested even more so with Wilson, the reigning World Cup and Olympics MVP, and Plum no longer available. But they still have a core of experienced veterans in Stewart, Gray, Collier, Young and Copper, who know what it takes to win gold. -- Alexa Philippou

2. France
Current WNBA players:

G Pauline Astier, New York Liberty (9.2 PPG, 2.5 RPG, 3.4 APG)

F Valeriane Ayayi, Phoenix Mercury (6.3 PPG, 2.7 RPG, 1.3 APG)

G Marine Johannes, New York Liberty (8.5 PPG, 2.1 RPG, 2.4 APG)

G Leila Lacan, Connecticut Sun (11.6 PPG, 1.9 RPG, 4.6 APG)

G Carla Leite, Portland Fire (15.9 PPG, 2.1 RPG, 6.3 APG)

C Dominique Malonga, Seattle Storm (17.0 PPG, 9.0 RPG, 1.5 BPG)

F Janelle Salaun, Golden State Valkyries (12.9 PPG, 3.9 RPG, 1.2 APG)

G Gabby Williams, Golden State Valkyries (14.3 PPG, 3.3 RPG, 2.2 APG)

Other notable players: C Marieme Badiane

Outlook: France, seen as the top threat to Team USA, might have its most talented roster ever with eight active WNBA players, four of whom will be headed to the playoffs. France has been building as an international power for the last several years. The French nearly toppled Team USA in the Olympic final in Paris in 2024, falling 67-66 behind former UConn star Williams' 19 points. France also took Olympic silver in 2012 and bronze in 2021.

France's only medal in the World Cup was a bronze in 1953, the first year of the event, but they are expected to have a podium finish this year. Malonga, the 2025 No. 2 WNBA draft pick who dunked in the All-Star Game in July, might look to do that in the World Cup. -- Michael Voepel

3. Spain

Current WNBA players:

G Elena Buenavida, Minnesota Lynx (developmental player)

C Raquel Carrera, New York Liberty (1.4 PPG, 1.1 RPG, 0.3 APG)

F Maria Conde, Toronto Tempo (8.9 PPG, 4.6 RPG, 2.6 APG)

C Megan DiLeo, Portland Fire (13.2 PPG, 4.2 RPG, 0.6 BPG)

C Awa Fam, Seattle Storm (10.3 PPG, 5.7 RPG, 0.9 SPG)

G Alicia Florez, Washington Mystics (3.3 PPG, 2.0 APG, 0.6 SPG)

Other notable players: G Iyana Martin, G Maite Cazorla

Outlook: Spain has had a relatively quiet output on the international stage in recent years. They medaled at the World Cup in 2010, 2014 and 2018 and took silver at the 2016 Olympics -- but then didn't even qualify for the previous World Cup in 2022 or the podium in Paris.

Coming off a silver-medal finish at last year's EuroBasket -- and more recently giving the USA its closest game of March's qualifying tournament -- Spain could be poised for a big showing in Berlin. The team is led by veteran Alba Torrens, the only player with World Cup experience, and has a naturalized star in DiLeo, who was a top-five scorer at the 2024 Olympics. Carrera has seen limited time with the Liberty but has been much more productive with her national team. What might be most anticipated, though, is the emergence of Spain's young tandem of 20-year-old stars in Storm rookie Fam and Martin, the Fire's draft-and-stash first-round selection. -- Philippou

4. Belgium

Current WNBA players:

G Julie Allemand, Toronto Tempo (6.3 PPG, 3.1 RPG, 5.6 APG)

C Kyara Linskens, Phoenix Mercury (3.0 PPG, 2.4 RPG, 0.7 BPG)

F Antonia Delaere, Minnesota Lynx (2.9 PPG, 0.7 RPG, 1.1 APG)

Other notable players: F Emma Meesseman, G Julie Vanloo, F Bethy Mununga

Outlook: Belgium should be one of the powers of Group C, along with Australia. The Cats are coached by longtime former WNBA coach Mike Thibault, who won a title with the Washington Mystics in 2019 when Meesseman was WNBA Finals MVP. Meesseman has played nine seasons in the WNBA, most recently last year when she spent 20 games (including the playoffs) with the New York Liberty. Vanloo played briefly (five games) with the Liberty this season. This is Allemand's fourth season in the WNBA, and she has been a starter for the expansion Tempo. This is Belgium's third World Cup appearance; they finished fourth in 2018 and fifth in 2022. Belgium has not medaled at the Olympics but had its best finish in Paris in 2024, falling in the bronze medal game. -- Voepel

5. Germany

Projected WNBA players:

F Frieda Buhner, Portland Fire (6.3 PPG, 2.2 RPG, 0.7 APG)

G Leonie Fiebich, New York Liberty (10.2 PPG, 3.0 RPG, 1.1 SPG)

C Luisa Geiselsoder, Portland Fire (4.5 PPG, 2.6 RPG, 1.3 APG)

F Nyara Sabally, Toronto Tempo (12.3 PPG, 5.3 RPG, 0.9 BPG)

* Roster not yet finalized

Outlook: Just like in the Olympics, a World Cup host faces a mixture of pressure and opportunity, and it's no different for Germany in what is just its second time participating in the event (and first since 1998). Unfortunately the Germans will be without the services of star Satou Sabally, who has stepped away from basketball while recovering from the effects of her second concussion in eight months, and it's unclear how healthy her sister, Nyara, will be. For the Germans to earn their first podium finish at a major international competition, they will need a huge tournament from Fiebich, who has been showcasing her value with the Liberty upon returning from injury. But also expect the likes of Buhner and Geiselsoder to play even bigger roles than they do stateside in Portland. Germany is coached by Olaf Lange, current Tempo associate head coach and Sandy Brondello's husband. -- Philippou

6. China

Projected WNBA players:

C Han Xu, New York Liberty (6.4 PPG, 2.6 RPG, 0.7 BPG)

* Roster is not yet finalized

Outlook: China should be the toughest challenger to Team USA in Group D, and the two play in the event opener for both. But the team was dealt a blow Wednesday when 6-foot-7 Dallas Wings center Li Yueru said on social media she will not be competing in Berlin because her passport was lost in the mail.

The United States and China faced off twice at the 2022 World Cup, with the U.S. women winning by 14 in group play and by 22 in the gold medal match. That result was still a win for the Chinese, though, as it marked the first time since 1994 that they earned a medal at a major international competition (both were silvers).

China faltered at the 2024 Olympics, finishing in ninth, before punching its ticket to the World Cup at this spring's qualifying tournament in Wuhan. This roster has some new faces compared to that '22 squad, headlined by the 7-foot-2, 19-year-old Zhang Ziyu. But she's not the only player who could pose some trouble for the USA, as the more experienced Han Xu (6-11) brings additional height. -- Philippou

7. Australia

Current WNBA players:

F Chloe Bibby, Minnesota Lynx (2.3 PPG, 0.7 RPG, 0.7 BPG)

G Isobel Borlase, Atlanta Dream (4.6 PPG, 1.5 RPG, 1.0 APG)

C Ezi Magbegor, Seattle Storm (6.9 PPG, 4.0 RPG, 1.2 BPG)

G Jade Melbourne, Seattle Storm (9.5 PPG, 2.2 RPG, 3.9 APG)

F Alanna Smith, Dallas Wings (6.0 PPG, 3.9 RPG, 1.0 APG)

G Miela Sowah, Golden State Valkyries (0.3 PPG, 0.8 RPG)

F Stephanie Talbot, Las Vegas Aces (3.5 PPG, 2.6 RPG, 1.0 APG)

Other notable players: F Alex Fowler, G Alex Wilson

Outlook: Phoenix Mercury guard Sami Whitcomb, captain of the Australian team, had to withdraw from the World Cup last week because of an ongoing knee injury. It's a big blow to the Opals regarding leadership and scoring. And it's heartbreaking for Whitcomb, who is 38. She was replaced by Sowah, 26. Sandy Brondello, who won WNBA titles with the Mercury (2014) and New York Liberty (2024) and is now with the Toronto Tempo, is Australia's coach.

The Opals began to emerge as an international power in women's basketball in the 1980s and won their first World Cup medal with a bronze in 1998. Their highlight was 2006, when they defeated Russia for the gold medal after the Russians had upset the United States in the semifinals. They also won bronze in 2002, 2014 and 2022, and took silver in 2018. Australia's six total World Cup medals puts them third on the all-time medal chart. The Aussies also have six Olympic medals: three silvers and three bronzes. -- Voepel

8. Italy

Current WNBA players:

G Costanza Verona, Dallas Wings (developmental player)

F Cecilia Zandalasini, Golden State Valkyries (8.8 PPG, 2.2 RPG, 1.8 APG)

Other notable players: F Lorela Cubaj

Outlook: Italy is enjoying a resurgence on the FIBA stage: Last year the team won its first EuroBasket medal since 1995 by beating France for the bronze medal, and now this World Cup marks the country's first appearance at a major international competition since the 1996 Olympics. Led by Zandalasini, the Italians lost 93-59 to the United States at the qualifying tournament in Puerto Rico, but went 4-1 overall at the event, including upsetting Spain the day after playing the U.S. women (and it's largely the same squad Italy has in Berlin). Italy has a difficult path ahead, though, having to face both the USA and China, the 2022 World Cup silver medalist, in the group phase. -- Philippou

9. Nigeria

Projected WNBA players:

F Amy Okonkwo, Portland Fire (4.3 PPG, 1.0 RPG, 0.3 APG)

* Roster not yet finalized

Outlook: This is the fourth time Nigeria has qualified for the World Cup, although it withdrew in 2022. That was much to the chagrin of the Nigerian players and FIBA. It was a decision by the Nigerian government, which opted in May 2022 to withdraw all its basketball teams from international competition while it restructured the sport's governance. Nigeria earned its World Cup berth this time by winning the AfroBasket 2025 championship. The team still played in the World Cup qualifying tournament in France in March, but lost three of five games. Nigeria's best finish in the World Cup is eighth, in 2018. The team's best Olympic finish is also eighth, in 2024. -- Voepel

10. Japan

Current WNBA players:

G Mai Yamamoto, Las Vegas Aces (5.8 PPG, 1.8 APG, 0.8 SPG)

Other notable players: G Rui Machida, G Kokoro Tanaka, C Ramu Tokashiki

Outlook: American basketball fans have come to enjoy Japan's entertaining style of play in recent years, particularly since squaring off against the USA in the 2020 Olympic gold medal game. Japan is known for speed, movement and 3-point shooting, which means the team can beat anyone if it gets hot -- and can lose to anyone if it can't hit shots. Lack of size is often an Achilles' heel -- just one player, Tokashiki, is listed over 6-foot.

Still, look out for the likes of Yamamoto, a midseason addition to the Aces, as well as Golden State draft pick Tanaka to make a splash on the perimeter. After the high of clinching silver at the Tokyo Olympics, Japan finished ninth at the 2022 World Cup, 12th at the Paris Olympics and almost didn't qualify for Berlin. Corey Gaines, the coach of the 2009 Phoenix Mercury championship squad, took over as head coach in early 2025. The pressure is on for them to find their form going into 2030, when they will host the next World Cup. -- Philippou

11. Hungary

Projected WNBA players:

F Dorka Juhász, Minnesota Lynx (3.8 PPG, 2.6 RPG, 1.2 APG)

* Roster not yet finalized

Outlook: While France is a big favorite in Group B, Hungary might make some waves behind Juhász. That especially could be the case with JiSu Park out for Korea and Nigeria looking kind of inconsistent entering the tournament. Hungary is making its sixth appearance in the World Cup but first since 1998. The team's best finish was fifth in 1957. -- Voepel

12. Korea

Current WNBA players:

G Jihyun Park, Los Angeles Sparks (2.2 PPG, 1.0 RPG, 0.5 APG)

Outlook: Korea is typically known as a strong outside shooting team. The team will need to rely even more on its guards with center JiSu Park, who played three seasons with the Las Vegas Aces, out due to an ankle injury. Korea is making its 18th World Cup appearance; it has played in every tournament except the first two in 1953 and 1957. Korea has won two silver medals, in 1967 and 1979. The team also has finished fourth three times, most recently in 2002. Korea has one medal in Olympic play, a silver in 1984. -- Voepel

13. Türkiye

Projected WNBA players:

G/F Kennedy Burke, Connecticut Sun (8.8 PPG, 3.2 RPG, 1.4 APG)

* Roster not yet finalized

Outlook: Türkiye will learn a lot about its chances from its opener vs. Belgium. This is Türkiye's third appearance in the World Cup; the team was fourth in 2014, when it hosted the event, and 10th in 2018. In her seventh year in the WNBA, Burke is having a career-best season. -- Voepel

14. Mali

Projected WNBA players:

G Aicha Coulibaly, Chicago Sky (4.8 PPG, 2.8 RPG, 0.7 SPG)

F Sika Kone, Atlanta Dream (1.7 PPG, 1.0 RPG)

* Roster not yet finalized

Outlook: Mali will make its third World Cup appearance, where it hopes to improve on an 11th-place finish in 2022. The program established itself as the second-best team out of Africa behind Nigeria, which beat Mali in the 2025 AfroBasket final. But Mali followed that up with a promising showing during the qualifying tournament in March, beating Czechia and narrowly losing to Brazil to clinch a spot in Berlin. Maimouna Haidara was the team's leading scorer in Wuhan, followed by the Dream's Kone; they'll need those two to dazzle to cause some upsets in Group A. -- Philippou

15. Czechia

Current WNBA players:

G Eliska Joklova, Minnesota Lynx (1.7 PPG, 1.1 APG, 1.0 RPG)

Outlook: Czechia is back at the World Cup after last appearing in the event in 2014; in 2010, it was the host nation and earned silver. The team's return this year has already been met with some concern. Czechia eked into the World Cup after a tepid qualifying tournament and has had some bad injury luck to two key players: Emma Cechova tore her ACL three games into her season with the Minnesota Lynx after a promising start, while Julia Reisingerova is also unavailable due to injury. On top of that, Czechia has to face the United States, China and a surging Italy squad in group play. It'll need sensational outings from the likes of Lynx rookie Joklova (née Hamzova), Veronika Vorackova and Petra Holesinska to keep up. -- Philippou

16. Puerto Rico

Current WNBA players: None

Other notable players: G Arella Guirantes, C Imani McGee-Stafford

Outlook: Host Puerto Rico was fourth in the qualifying tournament won by the United States in March in San Juan. A tough group awaits in Berlin, especially having to face Australia and Belgium. This is Puerto Rico's third appearance in the World Cup, having finished 16th in 2018 and eighth in 2022. Guirantes played two seasons in the WNBA, most recently in 2023. McGee-Stafford played four seasons in the league, most recently in 2019. Puerto Rico has competed twice in the Olympics. -- Voepel

Groups

Sixteen teams will compete in the FIBA World Cup in Berlin, Germany, with 36 games being played over 10 days from Sept. 4 to Sept. 13. The first-place team in each group advances to the quarterfinals; the second- and third-place teams will qualify for a single-game elimination format to determine the rest of the quarterfinalists.

stories.headline: Blues name Thomas as captain despite last season's trade rumors
stories.summary: The Blues have named center Robert Thomas as the 25th captain in franchise history just months after his name was heavily circulated in trade rumors.
stories.body:
The St. Louis Blues have named center Robert Thomas as the 25th captain in franchise history, months after his name was heavily circulated in trade rumors.

Thomas, 27, led the Blues with 64 points (25 goals, 39 assists) in 64 games last season, skating to a plus-22. Thomas has 132 goals and 328 assists in 530 career games. He's entering his ninth NHL season after being selected by St. Louis 20th overall in the 2017 NHL draft. Thomas will become the seventh original Blues draft pick to be named captain.

Thomas replaces Brayden Schenn as captain, who was traded to the New York Islanders at last season's deadline.

Defensemen Colton Parayko and Philip Broberg, and forwards Jake Neighbours and Dylan Holloway, will be named assistant captains for the 2026-27 season at a news conference Thursday.

Thomas is signed through the 2030-31 NHL season with an average annual contract value of $8.125 million. He has a full no-movement clause until the last year of his contract, but that didn't stop his name from whirling through the rumor mill last season. The Minnesota Wild and Buffalo Sabres were among the teams that made offers for Thomas, but those talks never reached the point where the Blues asked Thomas to waive his trade protection.

stories.headline: State of Origin: Darius Boyd replaces Billy Slater as Queensland coach
stories.summary: Darius Boyd will replace Billy Slater as Queensland's State of Origin coach after impressing in his role with the Maroons under 19 team.
stories.body:
Former Queensland star Darius Boyd is the new Maroons coach after being appointed to take over in 2027.

The Queensland Rugby League confirmed on Thursday that Boyd would take up the position on a two-year deal after Billy Slater stepped down from the role after a five-year stint.

Boyd, who won NRL premierships with Brisbane and St George Illawarra in a 337-game career, played 28 State of Origin matches for the Maroons and was a key figure in the dynasty under coach Mal Meninga.

As a coach he has led the Queensland U19 team to wins in back-back interstate clashes after being a member of the coaching staff at the Broncos under Kevin Walters.

Boyd, who also played 23 Tests for Australia, said he was "extremely honoured" to be entrusted with coaching Queensland's State of Origin team.

"It's a privileged position and I'm very grateful for the opportunity," Boyd said.

"I understand the responsibility that comes with the role as well. My job is to build on the legacy created by the many great Queensland players and coaches who have come before us."

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- Chelsea have made contact with former Liverpool midfielder Georginio Wijnaldum, Footmercato has revealed. The Netherlands international has been a free agent since leaving Saudi side Al Ettifaq, meaning the Blues can sign him at any time. Wijnaldum is viewed as a backup option to Monaco's Lamine Camara, whose proposed €55 million move to Chelsea collapsed at the final hurdle on deadline day. With the transfer window not reopening until January, the 35-year-old Wijnaldum -- who is also wanted by several Saudi clubs -- could now be their best short-term midfield option.

- Chelsea will face competition from Liverpool if they revive their interest in Camara, says TalkSPORT. The Reds recently contacted Camara's representatives to express an interest in signing him next summer, if a move to Stamford Bridge doesn't materialize in January. The 22-year-old is viewed as a long-term replacement for Alexis Mac Allister, who was linked with Manchester City this summer.

- Arsenal are considering a January move for AFC Bournemouth forward Junior Kroupi, according to The Independent. The 20-year-old Frenchman was on the Gunners' radar throughout the summer, but Arsenal opted against pursuing a deal before the transfer window closed. Kroupi is highly regarded at the Emirates, and the club could revisit their interest when the window reopens in January as they look to add further attacking options. Atlético Madrid's Julián Álvarez is also a player of interest, and his relationship with the Spanish club may have deteriorated further by the time the window reopens.

- Newcastle United will continue their pursuit of Bayer Leverkusen striker Christian Kofane in January, says Football Insider. The 20-year-old was also wanted by Aston Villa, but neither club were able to complete a deal before the deadline. Kofane is viewed as a player with huge upside and fits Newcastle's new recruitment strategy of targeting high-potential players. The Cameroon international scored seven goals and provided six assists last season and has already netted twice this campaign.

- Richarlison has agreed personal terms to join Trabzonspor, according to Fabrizio Romano. The Tottenham Hotspur forward has reportedly agreed a salary worth three times his current earnings at the Premier League club. Trabzonspor have already seen bids of £15 million and £20 million rejected by Tottenham, but a new proposal is expected soon as the Turkish club make the Brazilian their priority target.

Formula 1 action is back in full swing and next up on the calendar is Monza, also known as the "Temple of Speed."

McLaren's Lando Norris sealed back-to-back victories after winning the Dutch Grand Prix to kick off the second half of the season last time out.

Kimi Antonelli is leading the championship by 59 points and following behind is his teammate George Russell and Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton both in second.

The Italian youngster will be hit with a grid penalty at his home race for taking a new engine.

So you don't miss a thing, here's everything you need to know about the Italian Grand Prix.

How to watch

Sky Sports has exclusive F1 rights again in 2026 in the U.K., with every session live on Sky Sports F1. The sessions are also on Sky Sports Main Event.

For non-subscribers, highlights of the Italian Grand Prix will be on free-to-air television on Channel 4.

In the U.S., subscribers can watch every session on Apple TV, via a new F1 channel on the platform.

Autodromo Nazionale Monza

The "Temple of Speed" is known for it's long straights and heavy braking zones, and is the fastest track in Formula 1 history by overall average lap speed.

It's another classic circuit that has been on the calendar since 1950, only missing one year of racing in 1980 due to upgrading the track infrastructure.

It has one of the best podiums in the world as the famous Ferrari-loving tifosi flood onto the track after the race is finished. It's always a sight to be seen, especially if you are a Ferrari driver or an Italian driver.

Italian Grand Prix

Circuit: Autodromo Nazionale Monza; Monza, Italy

2016: Nico Rosberg, Mercedes

2021: Daniel Ricciardo, McLaren

2022: Max Verstappen, Red Bull

2023: Max Verstappen, Red Bull

2025: Max Verstappen, Red Bull

Other key stats

First F1 race: 1950

Lap record: 1:18.792, Max Verstappen (Red Bull)

Laps: 53 laps of 5.8km. Total distance 306km

Most poles: Lewis Hamilton has seven at this circuit (2009, 2012, 2014-2017, 2020). Other pole sitters from the grid are Fernando Alonso (2007, 2010), Charles Leclerc (2019, 2022), Max Verstappen (2021 and 2025), Carlos Sainz (2023) and Lando Norris (2024).

Most wins: Lewis Hamilton (2012, 2014-2015, 2017-2018) and Michael Schumacher (1996, 1998, 2000, 2003, 2006) are tied on five wins each. Other winners from the current grid are Fernando Alonso (2007, 2010), Pierre Gasly (2020), Charles Leclerc (2019, 2024) and Max Verstappen (2022, 2023 and 2025).

Weather forecast

The weather for the Italian Grand Prix is forecast to be sunny all weekend with light winds, with highs of 32°C on Sunday.

What happened last year?

Max Verstappen set the pace with the fastest lap in F1 history after getting pole position in Monza.

The Dutchman set a time of 1:18.792 breaking Hamilton's record from 2020.

It was McLaren's Norris who was on provisional pole before Verstappen beat him to the line in the closing stages.

Verstappen then went on to win the race in commanding fashion, but there were some team orders taking place at McLaren.

Norris was running in second for the majority of the race, but after a slow pit-stop, the team asked Oscar Piastri to move aside and let him teammate back through for second place.

At the time, Piastri was leading the championship from Norris by 31 points.

Who will win this year?

The biggest news entering the weekend will be Antonelli's engine penalty that will hamper his opportunity to score maximum points during the race.

He leads the championship after winning six races, but title fights can change quickly, as we saw during the backend of the 2025 season.

McLaren's upgrades have certainly been working, but team boss Andrea Stella said that Monza will be the true benchmark in terms of its performance and progress.

Ferrari will be hungry to get a home win with either of its drivers, but Monza will typically suit those strong in straight line speed and high-speed corners, such as Mercedes.

Monza could be one of the best opportunities to close the gap in the title race and take advantage of Antonelli not being a threat at the front of the pack.

stories.headline: NBA punishes Clippers after Kawhi investigation: Top questions
stories.summary: A $30M fine. Five first-round picks taken away. Steve Ballmer suspended for a year. ESPN's NBA insiders break down the harshest punishment in league history.
stories.body:
The NBA has released the findings of its nearly yearlong investigation into the LA Clippers and Kawhi Leonard, punishing both for violating salary cap circumvention rules when the team signed Leonard to an extension in 2021.

The league released a statement Wednesday outlining that the investigation found "multiple significant rules violations by the Clippers organization."

Punishments include a $30 million fine and suspension for owner Steve Ballmer (one year), plus suspensions for team president of business operations Gillian Zucker (one year without pay) and president of basketball operations Lawrence Frank (six months without pay).

The Clippers must also forfeit first-round picks in 2029, 2030, 2031, 2032 and 2033. Add the picks sent to the Oklahoma City Thunder in 2019 to acquire Paul George and secure Leonard's free agent signing, and LA will have given up a total of 10 first-rounders to acquire and retain Leonard.

What does this all mean for Leonard, Ballmer and the future of the Clippers franchise? What will become of the agreed blockbuster trade to send the star forward to the Toronto Raptors?

ESPN's NBA insiders examine every angle of the league's shocking announcement.

How did the NBA come to this decision? How did it arrive at this punishment?
A significant part of this case appears to come down to the words "affirmative" and "responsive" as it pertained to how Leonard and the four companies arrived at endorsement deals.

In the investigator's report and in the Clippers' subsequent publicly released response, each side accuses the other of a flawed theory in how interactions between Leonard and the four companies were handled.

The Clippers believe their actions, connecting interested companies to Leonard for possible endorsement deals, constitutes a role as a middleman, which is permitted by league rules.

The investigators do not believe this and presented findings that they feel show the team flagrantly and repeatedly broke cap circumvention rules -- and that the Clippers took actions to make it appear, through emails, that they were acting within the rules.

The report repeatedly rejects the Clippers' argument that the connections were affirmative and, in some cases, cites admissions by the companies themselves.

The details make for compelling reading. In the case of scoreboard maker Daktronics, for example, the investigators accuse the Clippers of directing a kickback from a massive scoreboard contract for Intuit Dome to Leonard in the form of an endorsement deal and even setting the terms.

In other cases, the report cites the Clippers paying millions in "consulting" fees shortly after Leonard's endorsement deals were executed. The report doesn't specify exactly how the investigators acquired this information but repeatedly cites interviews with executives of the companies.

This punishment is in line with the penalty David Stern levied on the Minnesota Timberwolves in 2000 for executing an under-the-table deal with Joe Smith, which included five lost first-round picks, a then-record fine of $3.5 million, and owner and executive suspension and lost pay.

As for the size of the fine, the league appears to have imposed the maximum allowed fine for cap circumvention, $7.5 million, and imposed it for all four companies it believes the Clippers conspired with to circumvent cap rules, resulting in a compounded fine of $30 million. -- Brian Windhorst

Why did the NBA come down so hard on the Clippers if it didn't have "hard evidence" of salary cap circumvention?
The Wachtell report alleges Ballmer generally failed to "create conditions under which his organization abided by the NBA's circumvention rules."

It also says he "knowingly sought to help [Kahwi] Leonard obtain off-court income opportunities and, in at least one instance, engaged in a significant act of team facilitation."

However, the report cites no specific evidence that would appear to implicate Ballmer directly. Instead, it connects the dots using the Clippers' knowledge of demands from Leonard's representative, Dennis Robertson, introductions between the Clippers and their sponsors, and communications regarding the latter.

The official reason the NBA gave for its conclusions and the level of punishment is the number and depth of the salary cap circumvention violations over the length of time the Clippers are accused of committing them.

According to investigators, contemporaneous notes from Frank indicate that Robertson complained to Ballmer that Zucker, the president of business operations, was making "introductions" for "bulls--- deals," and that "I have to get paid."

Investigators cited the same notes as saying Ballmer told Robertson that Clippers staff were "collective workers to try and help [Leonard] achieve his financial goals."

In addition to the notes written by Frank, who appears to have been given leniency for his cooperation, the report cites information that appears to have come from interviews with executives from the involved companies that created a compelling case.

The punishment was compounded by the Clippers being previous offenders during Ballmer's tenure as owner. They were fined $250,000 for a similar accusation involving DeAndre Jordan in 2015. There was also a 2019 investigation into Leonard's signing in which they were cleared of wrongdoing but subsequently warned and put through a seminar to remind them of the rules.

This penalty is indeed harsh, but it could have been worse.

In the case of Joe Smith and the Wolves in 2000, his contract was voided and his Bird rights were vacated.

Leonard will have to write a sizable check -- $700,000 -- but will not be suspended, and his contract and Bird rights remain unaffected.

The Clippers and the Raptors will be allowed to move forward in their trade process, one league source said. If the trade moves forward, LA will acquire two first-round picks in the deal. -- Windhorst

Do the Clippers have any recourse?

In its announcement, the NBA said the league and the NBPA have agreed on the penalties and that they are final and binding for all parties.

In a statement, however, the Clippers said they "intend to vigorously challenge these findings and penalties through every avenue available to us and look forward to an ethical and impartial arbitration process."

Ballmer's attorney, David Kelley, wrote an additional statement to the league, saying, "We are exploring every legal remedy to address this gross injustice."

Ballmer certainly has the means to commit resources toward clearing the team's name, though it's not immediately clear what those paths look like.

But it's not surprising that the Clippers would want to take this approach. They've been publicly and privately adamant from the start that they did not funnel money to Leonard through Aspiration, and one source close to the team with knowledge of the investigation said -- as ESPN previously reported -- that it would "fight that to the end," including through arbitration. -- Baxter Holmes

What does this punishment mean for the Clippers' future?
It means the Clippers have no access to first-round capital to use in a trade.

Trading center Ivica Zubac to the Indiana Pacers last February began the Clippers' process of rebuilding their draft assets, which had been depleted because of the trades for Paul George in 2019 and James Harden in 2023.

The Clippers acquired two picks in the deal, including one that resulted in the selection of Keaton Wagler with the No. 5 pick in this year's draft.

Before the NBA penalties were handed down, the Clippers had seven first-round picks over the next seven seasons, including four that were tradable. However, because of prior trades, LA had no control of its own first until 2030 (the Thunder have swap rights in 2027, the 76ers own the Clippers' 2028 pick and have swap rights in 2029).

By losing five firsts (the 2029 pick coming from the Pacers, plus their own picks in 2030, 2031, 2032 and 2033), the Clippers' lone future picks are the less favorable of their own, Oklahoma City's, Denver's (if 6-30) in 2027 and the 2029 pick, none of which can be traded.

The Clippers, however, could be getting some draft relief relatively soon.

As part of the agreed-to trade to send Leonard to the Toronto Raptors, the Clippers were supposed to receive unprotected first-round picks in 2031 and 2033.

The Clippers would not be allowed to trade those picks in future deals even if the Leonard trade goes through, because of the NBA's Stepien rule, which states that no team may trade a future first-round pick if the result would leave the team without first-round picks in any two consecutive future years. -- Bobby Marks

What does this mean for Steve Ballmer?
Ballmer has publicly and privately vowed to fight the NBA's decision, but it remains unclear what his options are outside of the court system. It's also unclear yet whether the NBA's yearlong suspension for Ballmer takes effect immediately, or whether he could ask the courts or an arbitrator to step in before it begins.

The alternate governor of the Clippers is Ballmer's business associate, Dennis Wong, who owns 1% of the team. Wong was named as an investor in Aspiration but is not mentioned in the release from the NBA on Wednesday.

This does not mean that Ballmer will have to sell the team, like former owner Donald Sterling did after being banned for life by NBA commissioner Adam Silver in 2014. Technically, Sterling did not have to sell the Clippers either. His wife, Shelly Sterling, decided to sell the team before the NBA's board of governors could vote to remove him as owner. -- Ramona Shelburne

Is there precedent for a team to be without its owner for an entire year?
Yes.

As part of the punishment from the Joe Smith salary cap circumvention case in 2000, the NBA suspended then-Minnesota Timberwolves owner Glen Taylor for one season. General manager Kevin McHale was also suspended for one season.

Other owners who have been suspended for a year or more for reasons other than salary cap circumvention include Donald Sterling (Clippers), Mark Stevens (Golden State Warriors) and Robert Sarver (Phoenix Suns). -- Marks

What does this mean for Lawrence Frank? Who is running the Clippers' front office in the interim?
The Clippers have not accepted the punishment and, therefore, have not named an interim leader of basketball operations.

However, it is likely that general manager Trent Redden, a respected veteran executive, will lead basketball operations.

If Frank is forced to sit out the next six months, the suspension will take him past the 2027 trade deadline but allow him to return in time for the draft, when the Clippers will have a first-round pick.

In that scenario, he will also be back in charge for 2027 free agency, when the Clippers are projected to have up to $50 million in salary cap space. -- Windhorst

Who is Gillian Zucker? What was her role?
Zucker has been the head of business operations for the Clippers since Ballmer bought the team, and she was the point person on all four deals between the team sponsors who also had endorsement contracts with Leonard.

The report from Wachtell comes down harshly on her, concluding "when interviewed, she made misleading and false statements to investigators."

In one particularly detailed section of the report, investigators wrote that when Aspiration co-founder Joseph Sanberg told her he wanted to explore an endorsement agreement with Leonard, she "told Mr. Sanberg that she would enlist a particular business agent to assist Mr. Sanberg in structuring the agreement -- a business agent who was then under a retention agreement with the Clippers."

One day later, the report concludes that Zucker reached out to the business agent to help Sanberg.

That agent then emailed internal colleagues about the deal -- that Sanberg would offer Leonard $5 million, plus $7 million in stock, per year for four years as long as Leonard was with the Clippers.

The investigators concluded that Zucker improperly conveyed to the agent the proposed financial terms contained in this email.

The agent told investigators that neither the agent nor the agent's internal team came up with those terms. All relevant witnesses [including Zucker] agreed that Sanberg could not have come up with those terms because he didn't have experience structuring player endorsement deals. -- Shelburne

What does this mean for Dennis Robertson?
The NBA announced that Robertson, who has been a controversial figure in league circles for years, will face a five-year ban "from conducting business or otherwise engaging with NBA teams and their affiliates on behalf of or with respect to any player, employee, or other league or team personnel."

Robertson is Leonard's uncle and for years served as his business adviser.

He was also directly involved in Leonard's dealings with teams, including -- most notably -- his free agency negotiations with teams in 2019, during which Robertson made improper asks of the Clippers, including part ownership of the team, access to a private plane, a house and guaranteed off-court endorsement money, one source with direct knowledge of the talks previously told ESPN.

They were the same requests that, according to The Athletic, Robertson made of the Lakers and the Raptors. The Toronto Star reported Sept. 9 that Robertson also asked the Raptors for ownership stakes in outside companies and corporate sponsorship deals in which Leonard wouldn't have to do anything in return for the money.

These verbal requests fell outside the boundaries of the league's collective bargaining agreement, and word of them made waves around the league -- and reached the league office.

"As a direct result of Mr. Robertson's conduct on behalf of Mr. Leonard and the controversy surrounding the player's signing with the Clippers," the report from Wachtell Lipton noted Wednesday, "the NBA enacted a 'rules enforcement initiative' intended to promote better awareness, compliance, and enforcement of the circumvention rules.

"Among other things, this initiative included the adoption of the following rule:

"Teams are required to report to the league office any solicitation by a player of compensation or other benefits that are not authorized under the CBA. This includes any solicitation made by a player himself, by the player's agent, or by any other person acting (or purporting to act) on the player's behalf. Reports must be made even if the solicitation is rejected."

In July, ESPN's Shams Charania reported that Leonard hired Harrison Gaines of Slash Sports as his new agent and as someone who would lead all his business affairs. Gaines replaced Leonard's previous agent, Mitch Frankel, and the informal role that Robertson previously held.

In his statement Wednesday, Leonard alluded to Robertson in the opening paragraph:

"Integrity and respect for this game are fundamental to who I am. I accept full responsibility for lapses in judgment by people within my inner circle and regret the distraction this situation has caused the fans and my family." -- Holmes

Is there precedent for the Clippers to get some of their picks back?
Yes.

In 2000, Minnesota lost its next five first-round picks for violating salary cap circumvention rules with its illegal attempt to sign Joe Smith.

Three years later, however, the NBA gave the 2003 and 2005 first-round picks back to the Timberwolves, leaving them without picks in 2001, 2002 and 2004. -- Marks

stories.headline: Reports: Man charged in attempted burglary of Barkley's home
stories.summary: A 24-year-old man has been arrested and charged with multiple felonies in collection with an attempted break-in at the home of Eagles running back Saquon Barkley and two other burglaries.
stories.body:
A 24-year-old man has been arrested and charged with multiple felonies in collection with an attempted break-in at the home of Philadelphia Eagles running back Saquon Barkley and two other burglaries.

The Montgomery County District Attorney's Office announced Wednesday that Jabir Parker of Philadelphia was arrested Tuesday by the Lower Merion Police Department with assistance of FBI SWAT, the Pennsylvania State Police, the Philadelphia Police Department and the Pennsylvania Attorney General Office. He was charged with conspiracy to burglary, criminal trespass, theft by unlawful taking, receiving stolen property, criminal use of a communications facility and related crimes.

The news release from the Montgomery County DA doesn't identify Barkley's residence as the location of Parker's attempted burglary. However, multiple media outlets in Philadelphia, citing sources, reported that the residence in question belongs to Barkley and his family.

Parker is being held on $1 million bail. Additional suspects are being sought, according to authorities.

Barkley and his family were unharmed after the attempted burglary of their home, when they were inside the residence, on July 18.

Parker is alleged to have burglarized two other residences and stealing items of jewelry valued at nearly $800,000 as well as a safe.

The investigation used cellphone data, surveillance video and multiple interviews to identify Parker, the Montgomery County DA's office said.

stories.headline: Which fantasy hockey league is right for you?
stories.summary: Roto vs H2H points? Dynasty vs redraft? With all the scoring settings, roster setup and more, here's your first stop when signing up for an ESPN Fantasy Hockey league.
stories.body:
So you've decided to take the fantasy hockey plunge, joining millions of others in enjoying one of the sporting world's best game within a game. Welcome. Or perhaps you've already waded through these puck-friendly fantasy waters and feel inspired to dive into a different type of pool. Preseason greetings to you too. Either way, leaving other customizable options (roster size, lineup rules, bench flexibility, IR spots etc.) alone for now, here's a rundown of ESPN Fantasy's variety of fantasy hockey leagues, available to suit any taste.

H2H Points

The most popular game in ESPN's fantasy hockey universe pits individual managers against others in weekly head-to-head fisticuffs with a slew of weighted points at stake. Most total points wins the week 1-0 - no fuss, no muss. While always customizable to your own statistical taste, our default 12-category game presents as follows:

Goals (G) 2
Assists (A) 1
Power Play Points (PPP) .5
Short Handed Points (SHP) .5
Shots on Goal ( SOG) .1
Hits (HIT) .1
Blocked Shots (BLK) .5
Goaltender Wins (W) 4
Goals Against (GA) -2
Saves (SV) .2
Shutouts (SO) 3
Overtime Losses (OTL) 1

In stride with this formula, skaters who shoot regularly, score plentifully, and contribute often on the power play, qualify as fantasy royalty. But those characters are limited in number. Once the elite are spoken for, especially on larger fantasy rosters, there's much to appreciate about prolific shot-blockers who also chip in on offense on occasion. Think defenseman Jacob Trouba. An evening's haul including an assist, three hits, four shots, and three blocked, and -- without much obvious fantasy fanfare -- he's racked up 3.1 fantasy points. An above-average haul by any fantasy measure.

Furthermore, not unlike in the living, breathing game itself, goaltending matters. There are too many fantasy points at stake to pooh-pooh the position. While having good goaltending won't ensure a triumphant turn by April, rolling out sub-mediocre players on weak teams most certainly guarantees the opposite. Doesn't matter who you have up front. Pay the role proper mind, or pay a sad fantasy price.

In considering any player, spending a few moments in assessing the individual, by doing a little bit of simple arithmetic -- what is their potential fantasy sum? -- is the most sure-fire way to earn rich fantasy dividends in H2H points leagues. Whether it's during the draft or in evaluating free agent/trade commodities through the season.

H2H Categories

Varying from the H2H points formula, so-called "each" category leagues also maintain a committed, loyal following. Managers engaged in this style of contest, where stat egalitarianism reigns, are best served by striving for competitive balance. Each category, in direct head-to-head competition, is equal to each other in that goals, hits, blocked shots, whatever-your-fantasy-fancy etc. counts towards the week's final score, accruing over the course of the season. You've earned 31 shots on goal and your opponent has 30? You win that category, full stop.

Again, margin of victory in individual categories, large or small, matters not. Beating your competitor in hits by a singular check carries equal weight to obliterating them in goals. Since defeating your direct rival 10-2 in a 12 category format is a significantly bigger victory than edging them 6-5-1, you want to give yourself a competitive chance in all/most aspects of the fantasy game. Top-tier, well-rounded players are extra valuable in battling for a favorable blowout, especially on small rosters. For example, Florida's Brady Tkachuk checks a bunch of valuable boxes, night in and night out, in fantasy leagues that reward both scoring and physical play. Loading up on specialists in one category is much less useful than in other forms of H2H play. A balanced smorgasbord of skilled contributors in all aspects of the game will provide you with the greatest chance of campaign-long success.

H2H Most Categories

This type of league operates in similar fashion to "each" category competition except whichever manager emerges with the weekly victory wins 1-0. You win the week or you lose it, regardless of final tally. A 6-5-1 win is just as good as 12-0. In this case, the strategy of loading up on players who satisfy most stats, as opposed to striving for balance across the fantasy board, has merit. If you're rocking out in eight or nine of 12 categories, maybe don't sweat penalty minutes, or time-on-ice or the like too much. Securing a few "slam-dunk" categories at the expense of one or two others makes greater sense in this particular brand of fantasy play. Please don't draft a singular skater with an impressive plus/minus at the expense of nailing down shots on net. You're only increasing your odds of losing both categories.

It also bears repeating: Goaltenders cannot be shrugged off in any brand of H2H league, including this type, when more than two categories are devoted to the position. Please don't try to convince yourself otherwise.

Rotisserie (Roto)

Interested in a slow-burn, largely unforgiving league that can't be won in the first few months of the season but certainly can be lost? Willing to accept the challenge of assembling a roster with little margin for weakness, similar to how it's done IRL? Then this brand of fantasy play might be for you. As with H2H Categories competition, constructing and maintaining a balanced fantasy squad is vital in Roto leagues. Only more so. In direct competition with every other manager at all times, striving for a share of points available based on standings in individual categories, squandering one or two can prove catastrophically costly.

Sitting top spot in goals or ATOI or hits etc. in a 12-team/10-category league translates into 12 of a possible 12 points. Sitting dead last converts into a single point. That's a massive gap. Which is why ranking worst or near-bottom in a couple of stats, and subsequently earning only a point or two of a maximum of 12, is difficult to overcome, regardless of how well you're faring otherwise. By no means a gateway league, Roto competition best suits managers with strong fantasy stomachs. But that also means victory, when achieved, tastes all the sweeter after such a season-long grind.

Season Points

The ESPN Fantasy version that most closely resembles the lesser-nuanced game of your elders, where everyone gathered at the pub for an evening, armed with a pen, paper, and magazine, and selected their players for the year. Teams accrued points based on scoring and goaltending, and whichever side finished with the highest total, won.

Of course, there are many ways to cyber-customize your points league with other categories, trades, free-agent acquisitions, roster limits, and varying lineup adjustment windows. Daily or weekly, it's up to you. But the founding philosophy remains the same: the best overall team by season's end sports the crown. While this style of league lacks the charm of despising another individual manager over seven exclusive days in head-to-head combat, it -- unlike classic roto leagues -- serves as an excellent introduction for newbie managers to get their feet wet. Especially those who don't want to devote as much time, at least to start.

Dynasty/Keeper vs. Single Season

There are advantages to both. While dynasty/keeper competition is more kindred to how real teams are run -- management doesn't get to start from scratch every year in the NHL -- with redraft leagues, there's the benefit of enjoying a clean slate the following season, no matter how badly a current campaign is unfolding. But there's inarguably a greater sense of satisfaction with enjoying fantasy success on the blades of a roster built over time, from rebuild to peak performance. In stricter dynasty leagues, where few bodies move in or out, it's often nifty to maintain relationships with players from their rookie debuts, well into the veteran years. For many then, keeper competition -- middle ground between an all-in dynasty and turn-the-page redraft play -- will suit you best. Selecting six to eight keepers every campaign is a common tact, still allowing for improvement from outside help at season's onset. No one's going to relinquish Connor McDavid as a keeper, but some very good players will inevitably re-enter the draft in these modified leagues.

Again, there's no right or wrong way to play ESPN Fantasy Hockey. Depending on how much time and energy you want to invest - from the bare minimum to managing your squad as a quasi part-time job - it's all about customizing whichever league feels most up your own fantasy alley. And enjoying this great game through a fun bonus lens from late summer until it all wraps up in the spring.

Ready to play? Sign up for free today!

stories.headline: Song Yadong KO's Umar Nurmagomedov in massive UFC upset
stories.summary: Song Yadong pulled off a massive upset by knocking out heavily favored Umar Nurmagomedov in the men's bantamweight main event of UFC Fight Night in Shanghai.
stories.body:
Song Yadong saved the greatest performance of his career for his home country, knocking out former title challenger Umar Nurmagomedov in the men's bantamweight main event of UFC Fight Night on Saturday in Shanghai.

Song (24-9-1, 1 NC), a nearly 5-1 underdog at DraftKings Sportsbook, dropped Nurmagomedov with a short right hand, drawing a roar from the crowd when the fight was waved off at 1 minute, 48 seconds of Round 2.

"I believe in myself, and my team believed that I would win this fight," Song said through an interpreter. "They told me I would knock this guy out, and I did it."

It was the second straight fight in China for Song and his second straight win by finish. His most recent knockout win had been in 2023.

Song, making his first appearance in Shanghai since his UFC debut at age 19 in 2017, walked out to a hero's welcome.

"Nine years ago, I wanted to show I could walk in this Octagon," he said. "Nine years later, I want to prove I am the best in the world. I am the best Chinese fighter in the world."

The knockout came after Nurmagomedov (20-2) ducked out of the way of a left hand and right into the path of a short right hand, which connected near his right ear and sent him limply to the canvas. Song delivered three finishing shots on the mat before the referee jumped in.

That sent Song running around inside the cage in celebration, where he nearly ran into Nurmagomedov's younger brother and cornerman, PFL lightweight champion Usman Nurmagomedov, who had rushed in to check on his fallen brother. Usman Nurmagomedov appeared to throw an elbow in Song's direction as the elated winner was running past.

Song climbed atop the cage to soak in the fans' cheers before jumping down outside the cage and running into the crowd to get hugs and high-fives from fans.

"Maybe not today, maybe not tomorrow, maybe not next month, but I will be the first male Chinese UFC champion," Song said through the interpreter, with the "male" designation a nod to countrywoman Zhang Weili, a two-time women's champion at strawweight.

Song, who trains in Sacramento, California, switched to English and yelled, "Give me the title shot!"

stories.headline: Roosters coach backs NRL wildcard weekend
stories.summary: Trent Robinson has defended his decision to rest nine players ahead of the NRL finals, but would be in favour of a wildcard weekend to fixture a break for the top teams.
stories.body:
Trent Robinson has defended his decision to rest nine players ahead of the NRL finals, but would be in favour of a wildcard weekend to fixture a break for the top teams.

The fourth-placed Sydney Roosters drifted to $7 outsiders after announcing they would rest James Tedesco, Daly Cherry-Evans and seven others from Friday's clash with South Sydney.

Following Sam Walker's injury, Robinson admitted there was a temptation to give new halves combination Cherry-Evans and Hugo Savala a dry run in the last weekend before finals.

"There was some thought around that, but I also trust the way that they both play," he said.

"They've both trained a lot together."

The upheaval on the Roosters' team sheet comes after Penrith memorably rested 16 players for the penultimate round of last season, while finals-bound Cronulla and the Warriors are also resting fit players this weekend.

The situation has reignited suggestions of introducing a pre-finals wildcard round.

That would allow the teams that finish between first and sixth to rest the weekend before finals and therefore play full strength until the end of the regular season.

The teams placed seventh to 10th, meanwhile, would play off to secure one of two finals spots, so would have incentive to name their best teams.

The AFL welcomed 172,769 fans to the two games across their first wildcard weekend last month.

It is understood NRL club chief executive officers were broadly in favour of introducing the concept when quizzed at Wednesday's meeting.

Robinson is also keen on introducing a wildcard weekend, but only once the league expands closer to 20 teams as it aims by the end of the decade.

"I think it makes commercial sense, I think it makes football sense as far as the weekend off and making the finals series at its best as well for those teams," he said.

"I think it's with some foresight not to (use it as we) go to 18 (teams), but probably going towards 20, and I think it's not all four of those teams getting into that finals series, it's only two of them.

"So you're not rewarding four teams, you're rewarding two teams that have to fight their way in."

Rex Bassingthwaighte, Toby Rodwell and Reece Foley all join the Roosters' starting backline with four NRL games of experience between them, while uncapped Hayden Barton, Aston Warwick and Jake Elliott are on the six-man bench.

Robinson insisted he was still taking the clash, between the NRL's two fiercest rivals, seriously.

"History will show that I love this game and respect this game, and I don't think there's any different this weekend, because Daly Cherry-Evans isn't playing and Toby Rodwell is," he said.

"There's a future in what we're going to be playing out there as well."

Rabbitohs coach Wayne Bennett shrugged at the Roosters' decision to rest players.

"I've done it before myself as a coach," he said.

"They know where they are in the competition and they're well placed, so it's not a bad time to give someone a rest if they need it."

Souths can secure a home final by defeating the Roosters and do not have a preference between hosting at Allianz or Accor Stadium.

Cronulla, meanwhile, are growing increasingly confident they will be able to host their home final at Shark Park despite its reduced capacity.

The Sharks are likely to finish fifth and face North Queensland, who are not expected to have a large enough contingent of travelling fans to warrant a bigger venue.
